newsitem.title: USA: American Eagle unit sells some operations.
newsitem.headline: American Eagle unit sells some operations.

text.p: American Eagle Group Inc said Friday its American Eagle Insurance Co (AEIC) subsidiary agreed to sell the inforce aviation business to Great American Insurance Co (GAIC).
American Eagle Group said in a news release that it was informed of the transaction from the unit's conservator.

The conservator informed the parent company that the deal will provide continued protection to American Eagle's inforce policyholders and provide additional resources for use by American Eagle for the benefit of its remaining policyholders and creditors, according to a news release.

The conservator terminated the positions of chairman, chief executve and chief financial officer as salaried positions of the insurance company subsidiary, effective August 1, in a bid to save money, the company said.
Philip Guthrie will retain his post as chairman, president and CEO at the parent company, and Richard Kurz will keep his post as CFO at AEG.
The company said the conservator is pursuing other capital and strategic alternatives to minimize cost and expenses while attempting to maximizing assets.
